page: Microsoft Azure D32ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 32 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

This server configuration includes 1890 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. The underlying AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 (specifically AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration features such as AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the D32ads_v6 demonstrates strong single-core and multi-core performance, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics. Memory performance is also strong, as reflected in high PassMark memory scores, while large-block uncached memory bandwidth reads and writes average 77.97 GB/sec and 55.91 GB/sec respectively. The system also excels in cryptographic operations and small-model LLM inference, while maintaining average performance in database operations, multi-threaded decompression, and static web serving.

Given its balanced resource density and high-capacity local NVMe storage, the D32ads_v6 offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring a mix of compute power and fast local disk access without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. It is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, relational databases, text and image processing pipelines, software compilation, and small-scale machine learning inference tasks.
